HackerRank arrays - minimum swaps: Given:
def minimum_swaps(arr):
    n = len(arr)
    visited = [False] * n
    swaps = 0
    for i in range(n):
        if visited[i] or arr[i] - 1 == i:
            continue
        cycle_size = 0
        j = i
        while not visited[j]:
            visited[j] = True
            j = arr[j] - 1
            cycle_size += 1
        swaps += cycle_size - 1
    return swaps
Every permutation decomposes into disjoint cycles (following each index to where its value belongs). A cycle of length k needs exactly k-1 swaps to resolve, so summing (cycle_size - 1) across all cycles gives the true minimum, no need to simulate actual swaps. O(n) time, O(n) space for the visited array.
HackerRank arrays - array manipulation::
def array_manipulation(n, queries):
    diff = [0] * (n + 2)
    for left, right, value in queries:
        diff[left] += value
        diff[right + 1] -= value
    max_value = running = 0
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        running += diff[i]
        max_value = max(max_value, running)
    return max_value
A difference array records only the start and end+1 of each range update in O(1) per query, then one final prefix sum pass reconstructs every element's true value and tracks the running maximum - O(n + q) total instead of O(n * q) from naively updating every index in every range.
HackerRank greedy - luck balance: Each c:
def luck_balance(k, contests):
    important = sorted((l for l, imp in contests if imp == 1), reverse=True)
    total = sum(l for l, imp in contests if imp == 0)
    total += sum(important[:k])
    total -= sum(important[k:])
    return total
All non-important contests should always be won (winning never costs luck for those), so their luck is added unconditionally. Among important contests, greedily lose the k with the highest luck values (losing subtracts nothing while winning would have required 'spending' effort, but algorithmically: you're allowed to lose k important ones, and losing the highest-luck ones maximizes total luck since a lost contest keeps its luck value while a won one is subtracted) - sorting descending and splitting at k is the greedy proof: any other choice of which k to lose can only be equal or worse.
HackerRank stack - largest rectangle: Gi:
def largest_rectangle(heights):
    stack = []
    max_area = 0
    for i, h in enumerate(heights + [0]):
        while stack and heights[stack[-1]] >= h:
            height = heights[stack.pop()]
            width = i if not stack else i - stack[-1] - 1
            max_area = max(max_area, height * width)
        stack.append(i)
    return max_area
Maintain a stack of indices with strictly increasing bar heights; when a shorter bar is encountered, pop and finalize the area for each taller bar just popped, since this new shorter bar is the first thing to its right that limits how far it could have extended. The width is computed from the gap between the new stack top (the nearest shorter bar to the left) and the current index. Each index is pushed and popped exactly once, giving O(n) time.
